title: Persistent odour from Kepong park a nuisance | The Star
text:
Persistent odour from Kepong park a nuisance | The Star
Residents say flood retention pond needs better outflow
VIsitors and residents around Kepong Metropolitan Park in Kuala Lumpur are calling for long-term solutions to the foul smell from its lake.
Regular visitors to the park said the problem has persisted for the past five years.
During a visit by StarMetro on May 24, a layer of green scum was visible on the surface of the lake, with an unpleasant odour detected around it.
Neoh Sing Chong, 69, who lives nearby, said the smell worsened significantly during dry spells.
“If it doesn’t rain for two consecutive days, the lake smells horrible,” he said.
“I used to take photos of birds here, but they are hard to spot these days since the odour started.
“If this goes on for another five to 10 years, the whole area will be affected,” he added.
Theresa Liu, 57, who exercises at the park regularly, said she now covered her mouth and nose when walking near the lake.
Neoh says the smell worsens during dry spells.
“Even my cousin, who lives on the 24th floor of a condominium near the park can smell it,” she said.
Liu urged Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) to clean the lake again.
Community activist Yee Poh Ping said the cause of the odour was due to lack of channels for water to flow out, which resulted in stagnant and polluted water.
“The lake is also a flood retention pond that receives dirty water from northern Kuala Lumpur and parts of Selayang,” he said.
Although DBKL has taken steps to address the issue since 2020, he said the efforts had been short-term and with limited results.
“Between 2020 and 2022, DBKL installed 10 aerators to improve water quality, but only marginal improvement was recorded.”
Yee noted four of the aerators were currently non-functional.
“In late 2022, DBKL placed a water pump at the lake to improve water flow, but the pipe ends in the middle of the lake without connecting to any outlet, so the dirty water just circulates back into the lake,” he said.
Yee suggested that DBKL build an additional culvert connecting the lake to a commercial drainage system outside the park, to improve water outflow.
“This method works. One of the existing culverts that links to a residential area at the other end of the lake keeps the water there cleaner and flowing,” he highlighted.
“We have suggested this to DBKL since 2020, but no action has been taken,” said Yee.
“Thousands of people visit the park on weekends, making it essential to ensure the lake and surrounding areas are well maintained,” he added.
DBKL has not responded to StarMetro’s queries on the matter as at press time.
